The role You will take ownership of the backend services powering the Rinn App, a digital lending platform enabling access to unsecured personal loans for salaried borrowers through partnerships with RBI-regulated lenders.
 The role involves working on TypeScript-based services across onboarding, KYC, underwriting, disbursal and repayment.

 Implement reliable integration mechanisms covering retries, idempotency, webhooks, error handling and reconciliation.
 Develop and maintain underwriting rules engines covering bureau-based checks, bank-statement analysis, versioned cohorts and A/B testing.
 Ensure accuracy and traceability of financial transactions, including ledger entries, repayment schedules, interest and fee calculations, and daily reconciliation with payment partners.

We are a Singapore-based company working across Australian hospitality businesses, marketing, and internal business systems.

We're looking for a developer who can build reliable software, understand how a business operates, and take ownership of problems from investigation through to completion.

This is not a coding-heavy role. It involves significant non-technical work, including coordinating with onsite staff, follow-ups, video editing and administrative tasks (you will be trained). Fluent English communication is a must and a dealbreaker.

You will work with senior developers and business leaders on OpenClaw, AI engineering, AI automation, and day-to-day operations. You'll learn workflows firsthand, help execute them, identify what needs improving, and build solutions for the repetitive parts.

Development and operations are both core responsibilities. You should be comfortable moving between coding, investigating operational issues, coordinating with colleagues, and following up until work is complete.

What You'll Work On

Business Operations

- Learn how our hospitality, customer service, marketing, and internal teams work.

- Handle assigned operational tasks directly and identify opportunities to improve or automate them.

- Monitor systems such as GoHighLevel, Goki, email, and booking platforms for missed messages, delayed responses, and unresolved issues.

- Coordinate with colleagues and operational teams, track progress, and follow up until issues are resolved.

- Keep task lists, documentation, and handovers organised.

- Support tasks outside development when needed, including AI-assisted video editing, creative support, research, and administrative follow-ups.

You do not need experience with every platform listed. You do need the initiative to learn, ask useful questions, and make progress independently.

Required Skills and Qualities

- Strong practical development skills in Python or JavaScript.

- Experience building backend services, REST APIs, and third-party integrations.

- Experience integrating AI/LLM APIs into applications or workflows.

- Confidence using Linux, Git, and the command line.

- Ability to develop, debug, test, and deploy your work.

- Fluent spoken and written English (mandatory), including the ability to explain problems to nontechnical colleagues.

- Strong organisation, prioritisation, and follow-through.

- Ability to investigate unfamiliar problems and propose practical next steps.

- Willingness to learn new tools and take responsibility beyond your main programming specialisation.

- Professional, empathetic communication with colleagues and operational teams.

We assess both technical ability and how you approach real business problems.

Nice to Have

- Next.js, Express, or Flask.

- VPS infrastructure.

- WordPress or WooCommerce.

- Workflow automation and internal tooling.

- GoHighLevel, hospitality systems, or booking-platform integrations.

- Experience in operations, customer service, project coordination, freelancing, or running your own projects.

Working Days, Hours and Expectations

This is a six-day role, Monday to Saturday. Saturday is a regular working day.

Typical India working hours are approximately 4:30 AM–12:30 PM IST, aligned with Australian business hours.

You should start your shift prepared, organise your priorities, and manage assigned tasks without repeated reminders. Raise blockers early and communicate clearly about progress and next …

UBQ.io is a global technology service provider dedicated to building a more sustainable, independent, and equitable future. We partner with global companies across industries, including AI, blockchain, software, biotech, and education, to transform bold ideas into real, meaningful solutions.

 Solid professional experience with Python, including building backend services or data applications.

 Clear communication, and the confidence to challenge and clarify requirements with finance teams.
 A MSc in Finance, or progress towards a professional qualification such as CFA or CAIA (Level I or above), or equivalent.

 Front-end experience with React and TypeScript, especially data-heavy UIs.

We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$400-US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.
 You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.
 Remote, any location. US$400-US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.
 How it works
 Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.
 Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.
 Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.
 Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.
 Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.
 Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.
 Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.
 

 Requirements
 2+ years of professional software engineering
 Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code)

 You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words
 At least 10 hours a week, starting now

 Nice to have
 Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure
 Experience building agent tasks or RL environments
 

 Terms
 Between US$400 - US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you
 Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms
 The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us

jobs.description:
## Why this role exists
Commenda helps companies operate across borders. We handle indirect tax, entity management, transfer pricing, and corporate tax and accounting for multinational businesses, so our customers can hire, sell, and operate in fifty jurisdictions without hiring fifty accountants.
That breadth is why we run as a multi-product company: each product has a GM with a pod of engineers. This model ships what customers ask for. It does not build the things no single pod owns:
* the customer and entity model every product reads from
* the document pipeline every filing runs through
* the integration layer that pulls in accounting data
* permissions and access control
* the AI infrastructure the pods build on
Left to the pods, those get built four different ways, or once and then never touched again.
Core Product owns that layer. The team reports to Adarsh, our Head of Product, who is an engineer and still writes code.
## What you'll own
### The shared primitives
The data models, services, integrations, and internal tooling every product is built on. Built once, built well, and documented well enough that a pod engineer can pick them up without finding you first. Part of the job is deciding what belongs in the core layer, which means telling a pod no when they want a special case.
### Surge capacity
Once or twice a quarter a project matters enough to the company that it outgrows the pod carrying it. You join, get to the shape of the problem fast, ship, and hand it back in better condition than you found it.
### The AI development lifecycle
We build with AI agents as a matter of course, and we want them to be good in our codebase. You'll structure the repo for agents, write the evals, define what "reviewable" means for agent-written code, and push on the tooling until the whole engineering org moves faster.
### Code quality
The standards, tests, and architecture that keep this a codebase people and agents can move fast in.
### Security
We hold customer tax and entity data across dozens of jurisdictions. Access control, tenant isolation, and audit all live in the core layer.
## How we'll judge it
* The shared systems work. When something breaks across products, it traces back to you and you fix it.
* The codebase gets easier to work in over time, for people and for agents. Clear boundaries, real tests, conventions that hold.
* Core systems absorb growth in customers, entities, and jurisdictions without a redesign, and without leaking data between tenants.
* Product teams use what you build instead of rolling their own. If they don't, that's a signal about your work.
* Customers get correct results on time. Every filing, registration, and calculation runs through the core layer.
## The week-to-week
This is a generalist role. In one week you might redesign the entity model, trace a cross-tenant permissions bug, and rewrite an integration's retry logic. You should want that. You'll form your own opinions and execute on them, with AI doing a lot of the work.

Hevo is a Series B data infrastructure company with $42M raised.
More than 2,000 companies across 40 plus countries use Hevo to move data from more than 150 sources into platforms such as Snowflake and BigQuery.
Our customers include DoorDash, Shopify, Pinterest, Postman and Icelandair.
Our engineering team is built in India, and so are the decisions.
We are not the remote engineering office of a US company.
The people building the product are the people deciding what to build.
 
What we are building:
We are building an AI system that creates data connectors by itself and keeps them working by itself.
No engineer should need to manually build every connector. No engineer should need to come back six months later because the source API changed.
Work that traditionally takes weeks or months should take hours. But building a connector is not the hardest part.
The real question is: Would you trust this system to run by itself, with nobody watching, for months?
That is the job.
What you’ll own as Associate SDE at Hevo:
Implement SaaS connectors for assigned applications, learning application specific nuances like basic auth and data extraction.
Assist in building simple REST API components, focusing on clean implementation and testing.
Debug and optimize code for data pipeline efficiency under mentorship.
Contribute to feature breakdown, coding, and documentation for smaller tasks.
Apply logical thinking to solve integration issues and improve component quality.
Build internal tools with AI for business teams to run their functions

Basic object-oriented programming skills and familiarity with design principles.
Exposure to data pipelines or APIs; eagerness to learn concurrency and performance basics.
Foundational knowledge of REST APIs (e.g., making calls, handling JSON) – no deep expertise needed.
Proficiency in Java/TypeScript/Python, good problem-solving with data structures and algorithms.
Strong analytical and logical thinking for real-world challenges.
 
Candidate Persona:
Freshers with experience in software development, ideally with internships in integrations or data tools.
B Tech in Computer Science or equivalent from a reputed college.
 
Why this role:
Very few teams are building autonomous AI systems that operate production infrastructure where being wrong has real consequences.
This is not a chatbot. It is infrastructure that has to remain correct, quietly, for months.
If that kind of problem excites you, there are not many places working on it this early.
You can talk to anyone in the company, including the CEO.
What you are trusted with depends on what you can do, not your title.

**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

The Data Services team within PDNA (Partner Data And Analytics) builds and operates the Agentic Data Platform that powers Amazon's Selling Partner analytics infrastructure. We serve 900K+ Selling Partners and 30K+ Amazonians through 4,000+ standardized metrics, real-time streaming pipelines validated at Black Friday scale (142M+ events), and the Curated Data Layer (CDL) — Amazon's strategic data infrastructure for Selling Partner GenAI applications including Seller Assistant, Supply Chain Expert, MCF, and ISS. We are building the future where intelligent agents autonomously operate data pipelines, serve analytics through MCP servers, and enable self-service insights at scale.  
  
You will build the infrastructure layer that sits between raw data and intelligent agents. Think of it as the operating system for agentic data — the MCP servers agents call, the query engines they reason through, the schema contracts they interpret, the streaming backbone they react to, and the validation services they trust. This is systems engineering applied to the agentic AI problem: you are not building agents — you are building the infrastructure that makes agents possible.  
  
Key job responsibilities  
1) Design and build MCP servers and data access APIs  
2) Engineer the real-time streaming backbone using Spark Structured Streaming, Kafka/MSK, Kinesis, and Lambda that powers agentic workflows.  
3) Build agent orchestration infrastructure — the tool registries, execution planners, state stores, and handoff protocols that enable specialized agents (ingestion, validation, delivery) to coordinate across the data operations lifecycle.
  
4) Develop trust and validation infrastructure that keeps agent-generated outputs reliable  
5) Extend the lakehouse for agentic consumption — building metadata contracts, schema registries, and catalog APIs on top of our Iceberg-based infrastructure that agents can reason over autonomously.
  
6) Own your systems end-to-end — design, build, test, deploy, operate, and document. Your infrastructure will be observable, self-healing, and resilient. You will participate in on-call, drive root-cause analysis, and permanently resolve operational issues.  
7)

Our portfolio includes trailblazer brands such as Cialfo, BridgeU, Explore, Kaaiser, EduGo, and Flow AI and which are dedicated to expanding global student mobility by serving their respective stakeholders in the ecosystem.

To create a world where every student, regardless of their ethnicity, nationality, socio-economic status, and learning preference, gets equal access to higher education through our world-class network of portfolio brands; a network that globally connects community stakeholders that provide the finest resources and support material, anywhere in the world and at any time.
 About Manifest Global:
 Manifest Global is building the infrastructure for global human capital mobility - connecting students, schools, universities, and employers across 50+ countries. Our portfolio spans Cialfo (AI-powered college counseling, 2,000+ schools), BridgeU (university guidance for international schools globally), Kaaiser (trusted study abroad counseling across India and Southeast Asia), and Explore (AI-powered university outreach, 1,000+ university partners). Together, we move talent across borders at scale. $80M raised. Still early.
What This Role Is
AI agents — systems that reason, plan, take action across tools, and complete real work end-to-end — have moved from research demos to production infrastructure in the last eighteen months. The companies that build them well will define the next decade of what software is and what people do.
Manifest Global sits at one of the most operationally complex intersections in the world. Every day, our platforms move students between continents, counselors between conversations, applications between deadlines, universities between recruiting cycles, and agents between thousands of families making generational decisions. The work is high-stakes, high-volume, and full of judgment calls — exactly the kind of work that breaks under brittle automation and exactly the kind of work AI agents, built properly, can transform.
That is the bet behind this role. Not chatbots. Not wrappers. Agents that actually do the work — drafting university shortlists with reasoning a counselor would defend, surfacing the right student profile to the right admissions officer, catching the document that's about to make an application fail before a human sees it. Agents that hold context across long workflows. Agents that know when to escalate and when to keep going. Agents that get measurably better as more of the network uses them.
You will build those agents across the Manifest portfolio, in production, at a scale that matters.
What Makes This Role Different
Most companies hiring AI agent builders right now have one of two problems. They have the data but no real product surface to deploy into, so the agents sit in demos waiting for distribution. Or they have the distribution but the underlying data is too fragmented to support agents that work in production. Manifest has both. Cialfo's 2,000+ schools, BridgeU's international school footprint, Kaaiser's three decades of placement data, Explore's 1,000+ universities — that is the substrate. Saige, already live inside Cialfo, is proof that AI in this domain works when it is built well. Your job is to extend that surface across the portfolio.
This is not a research role. The agents you build will be used by real counselors, students, admissions …

jobs.title: SDE2 - Full Stack
jobs.description:
About the role

We're hiring two backend-heavy full-stack engineers (SDE 2 or SDE 3) for the Cowork team at Sarvam. Cowork is the agentic side of Indus: users hand it real work, and an agent plans, uses tools and connectors, works in a cloud sandbox, and hands back files, docs and artifacts across web, Android, iOS, macOS and Windows.

The role is full stack, but the centre of gravity is the backend: the BFF that every client talks to, and increasingly the agent harness behind it. You'll ship features end to end, from the API and data model through to the client screens on mobile, desktop and web.

What you'll work on

Most of your time goes into the BFF and the services around it; the rest into client work and the harness, depending on what the roadmap needs that quarter.

 - BFF (Chat Service): design and own the APIs that web, mobile and desktop share: sessions, conversations, streaming turns, artifacts, connectors, custom and managed agents. Data modelling, migrations, auth and RBAC, pagination and search.

 - Real-time streaming: stream LLM output, tool calls and agent events from the harness to clients over an event bus, and keep it correct under reconnects, retries and partial failures.

 - Agent harness and platform: contribute to Panja, our agent harness: tool and MCP integrations, sandboxed execution, file and artifact flows, latency and token-cost work.

 - Clients: build features end to end on our Kotlin/Compose Multiplatform apps (Android, iOS, macOS, Windows) and the Next.js web app, so a feature you design in the backend reaches users on every surface.

 - Production ownership: observability, on-call, RCAs, and making the system faster and cheaper with numbers to back it.


Tech stack

Python and PostgreSQL are the core; you don't need every item below on day one.

 - Backend: Python, SQLAlchemy + Alembic, PostgreSQL, OpenAPI

 - Supporting services: Go

 - Mobile and desktop: Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform (Android, iOS, macOS, Windows)

 - Web: Next.js, React, TypeScript


What we're looking for

A strong backend engineer who has also shipped real frontend work and is happy to keep doing both.

 - 3+ years (SDE 2) or 5+ years (SDE 3) building and running production backend services.

 - Deep in at least one backend language; Python preferred, Go, Kotlin/JVM or TypeScript/Node also welcome.

 - Solid API and data-model design: REST/streaming APIs, PostgreSQL schema design, migrations, indexing, transactions.

 - Distributed-systems fundamentals: async processing, queues or event streams, idempotency, retries, failure handling.

 - Production experience on Kubernetes or a similar platform, with observability you actually used to debug an incident.

 - Has shipped user-facing features on at least one client platform: Android, iOS, desktop or web (React/Next.js). Kotlin/Compose experience is a plus, not a gate.

 - Willing to pick up the side of the stack they know less, and to learn agent and LLM systems on the job.

 - Clear written communication: design docs, PR descriptions, RCAs.

Nice to have

 - Built on LLM APIs: tool calling, streaming, prompt caching, evals, or an agent loop of your own.

 - MCP servers or clients, OAuth connector integrations, or sandboxed code execution.

 - Kotlin Multiplatform / Compose Multiplatform, or native Android/iOS.

 - Real-time systems: WebSockets/SSE, NATS, Kafka, or Temporal-style durable workflows.

 - Go services, or performance and cost work with measurable …
